prompt: In this course, gcloud compute machine-types list stops with "You do not currently have an active account selected". Where did the refusal happen?
hint: Was anything sent?

choices.text: At Google, which rejected the empty credentials it was sent
choices.why: Nothing was sent. gcloud checks for an account before it builds the request.

choices.text: On the laptop, in gcloud itself, before any request left
choices.why: Right. With no account selected, gcloud stops before the network is involved.

choices.text: In the Pub/Sub emulator, which does not know Compute Engine
choices.why: The emulator is not involved; gcloud did not try to reach anything.

choices.text: In Terraform, whose token no-account was used by gcloud
choices.why: gcloud does not read GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN for this; that variable is for Terraform.

prompt: Why does the lab export GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN=no-account in every terminal?
hint: What does Terraform need before it will plan, and what must it never have here?

choices.text: It is the token the Pub/Sub emulator expects from every client
choices.why: The emulator accepts clients with no credentials at all.

choices.text: It makes gcloud skip the account check for read-only commands
choices.why: gcloud still refuses without an account; the variable is read by Terraform.

choices.text: The provider needs a credential, and this one reaches no account
choices.why: Right. It satisfies the provider and would be refused by Google if it ever reached it.

choices.text: It is the free tier's shared token, valid for e2-micro machines
choices.why: There is no such token; the free tier needs a real account.

prompt: A plan stops with "could not find default credentials" and suggests gcloud auth application-default login. What does the course tell you to do?
hint: Which line of the terminal setup was skipped?

choices.text: Run the suggested login, since the plan reaches nothing anyway
choices.why: That puts a real credential on the laptop, one apply away from a billed machine.

choices.text: Delete the provider block, which is where the error points
choices.why: Without the block Terraform still configures the provider, and still needs a credential.

choices.text: Export GOOGLE_OAUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN=no-account in that terminal
choices.why: Right. The line was missing, and the word is enough for a plan.

choices.text: Run terraform init again so that the mirror is read
choices.why: init had worked; the plan stopped at credentials, not at the provider's installation.

prompt: The lab stands in for Google Cloud with gcloud, Terraform, the emulators and ___, which runs the containers Cloud Run would run.
hint: The tool from the course before this one.

prompt: Why are the course's prices typed into prices.py rather than downloaded by it, as AWS's list can be?
hint: What does Google's machine-readable catalogue ask for?

choices.text: The Cloud Billing Catalog API needs an API key, which needs an account
choices.why: Right. The public pages are readable by people, not by a program without credentials.

choices.text: Google forbids copying its prices into programs
choices.why: Nothing forbids it; the obstacle is that the machine-readable form needs a key.

choices.text: Google prices change every hour, so a download would be stale at once
choices.why: List prices do not move hourly. Spot prices change at most daily, and on-demand ones less often.

choices.text: A download would only give prices in Brazilian reais
choices.why: The catalogue quotes US dollars and other currencies; currency is not the obstacle.

prompt: The sheet prices e2-standard-4 at 0.13402284 USD an hour. What is a month of 730 hours, to the cent?
hint: Hourly price times 730.

prompt: The sheet's prices are Iowa's, and the lab places everything in São Paulo. What may the lessons safely do with them?
hint: Two numbers from the same page and day.

choices.text: Quote them as São Paulo's, since Google charges one price worldwide
choices.why: Prices differ by region; the sheet says which region it is.

choices.text: Add a fixed São Paulo surcharge to each of them
choices.why: No such fixed surcharge exists; each region has its own price list.

choices.text: Compare them with each other, all from one region and one day
choices.why: Right. A comparison needs consistent numbers; a budget needs your region's own page.

choices.text: Treat them as a bill for the lab's machines
choices.why: The lab runs nothing at Google and bills nothing.

prompt: Match each piece of the name c4a-highmem-8 to what it says.
hint: Series letter, generation, processor, ratio, count.

pairs.right: The performance tier of general purpose
About 8 GiB of memory per vCPU

right_distractors: Eight times the memory of a standard

prompt: How many vCPUs does n4-standard-16 have?
hint: Read the last word of the name.

choices.text: 4, because standard means 4 GiB per vCPU
choices.why: The 4 GiB is the ratio; the count is the last number.

choices.text: 64, four times the last number
choices.why: 64 is roughly its memory in GiB, not its vCPUs.

choices.text: It depends on the zone the machine is created in
choices.why: The zone decides whether the type is offered, not what it is.
Right. The last word of a predefined type is its vCPU count.

prompt: On an Intel series a vCPU is one hardware thread. What is it on c4a, Google's Arm series?
hint: Arm has no shared threads.

choices.text: A whole physical core
choices.why: Right. With no hyperthreading, a vCPU is a core, which is one reason the series matters as much as the size.

choices.text: Half a hardware thread, shared with a neighbour
choices.why: That would be a shared-core type, which is an E2 thing.

choices.text: Two hardware threads of one core, as on Intel
choices.why: On Intel a vCPU is one thread, and two of them share a core.

choices.text: A quarter of a core, with bursting above it
choices.why: That describes e2-micro's share, not an Arm vCPU.

prompt: terraform plan accepted machine_type = "e2-standard-3" and planned 1 to add. What does that tell you?
hint: Who holds the catalogue of machine types?

choices.text: That E2 offers three-vCPU machines in that zone
choices.why: E2 sizes go 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32; the plan did not ask the zone.

choices.text: Only that the file is coherent; Compute Engine checks the name
choices.why: Right. The provider checks the shape of the file, and the catalogue lives on the other side.

choices.text: That the provider rounds 3 up to the next valid size, 4
choices.why: The plan printed e2-standard-3 exactly as written; nothing rounds it.

choices.text: That the token no-account was accepted, so Google validated the plan
choices.why: Nothing reached Google; the plan ran in a lab with no network.

prompt: Terraform colours its output even into a pipe, so a plan you filter with grep is run with the flag -___.
hint: The flag removes the colour.

prompt: terraform init printed "(unauthenticated)" and a warning about incomplete lock file information. Why?
hint: Where did the provider come from?

choices.text: The token no-account was rejected while downloading
choices.why: Nothing was downloaded, and the token is not used by init.

choices.text: The provider binary was damaged on the way and should be reinstalled
choices.why: It installed and planned correctly; the message is about provenance.

choices.text: It came from the local mirror, so no registry signature was checked
choices.why: Right. The lock file holds checksums for this platform only, which is fine for a lab.

choices.text: HashiCorp only signs providers for paying customers
choices.why: Providers are signed for everyone; the mirror is why the check was skipped.

prompt: e2-highmem-2 is 65.99 USD a month and e2-standard-4 is 97.84. How much is saved in a year by running the first instead of the second?
hint: The monthly difference, times twelve.

prompt: Order these 2-vCPU, 8 GiB machines from the cheapest to the dearest, by the sheet.
hint: E2 is the cheapest; N2 is an older generation.
trap: c4a is a performance series and still comes before n4, because Arm is priced lower per vCPU.

prompt: A service runs on c4-standard-2. What has to be true before moving it to c4a-standard-2?
hint: What does the a in c4a change?

choices.text: The service must use more than 8 GiB of memory
choices.why: c4a-standard-2 has 8 GiB; memory is not the condition.

choices.text: The zone must offer sustained use discounts
choices.why: Discounts do not decide whether software runs.

choices.text: The project must move to a billing account set up for Arm
choices.why: There is no such account; billing does not care about processors.

choices.text: Its image and every compiled dependency must exist for arm64
choices.why: Right. C4A is Arm, and x86 binaries do not run on it.

prompt: A team's batch job is idle most of the night and, when it runs, waits mostly on a database. Someone proposes n4-standard-2 over e2-standard-2 "for the better processor". What is the strongest objection?
hint: What does the extra money buy, and when does that matter?

choices.text: Speed counts while computing, and this job spends its time waiting
choices.why: Right. N4 costs about 17 dollars more a month and buys speed this job does not use.

choices.text: N4 cannot attach a persistent disk at all
choices.why: N4 attaches Hyperdisk; lesson 3 compares the two families of disk.

choices.text: E2 is the newer of the two series, so it is the faster one anyway
choices.why: N4 is the newer series; E2 is the cheaper one.

choices.text: N4 machines are offered only in Iowa
choices.why: Availability varies by zone, but that is not the argument here.

prompt: Which family is meant for a database that keeps a terabyte in memory?
hint: Its letters are M and X.

choices.text: Compute optimised
choices.why: That is for arithmetic-heavy work.

choices.text: Accelerator optimised
choices.why: That carries GPUs.

choices.text: Memory optimised
choices.why: Right. It starts where general purpose stops, at around a terabyte.

choices.text: General purpose, highmem
choices.why: highmem is 8 GiB per vCPU, far short of a terabyte on any common size.

prompt: With N4 custom rates of 0.03275 USD per vCPU-hour and 0.003717 per GiB-hour, what does n4-custom-2-12288 cost an hour?
hint: 12288 MiB is 12 GiB.

prompt: n4-custom-4-32768 costs 182.46 a month and n4-highmem-4, with the same vCPUs and memory, 173.77. Why?
hint: What does Google's price page say about custom types?

choices.text: Custom types run on older processors
choices.why: Same series, same processors; the price differs, not the hardware.

choices.text: Custom types carry a 5% premium over predefined ones
choices.why: Right. A custom type that lands on a predefined shape is that shape, dearer.

choices.text: 32 GiB on four vCPUs is extended memory
choices.why: 8 GiB per vCPU is still inside N4's normal range.

choices.text: highmem prices include a sustained use discount already
choices.why: Both are on-demand list prices from the same page.

prompt: Why does a custom type's name carry its memory in MiB, as in n4-custom-4-10240?
hint: What unit does memory come in?

choices.text: MiB is cheaper per unit than GiB on the price page
choices.why: The price is per GiB-hour whatever the name says.

choices.text: Terraform rejects GiB in a machine_type string
choices.why: Terraform checks no names; the convention is Compute Engine's.

choices.text: It keeps the name shorter than writing GiB with decimals
choices.why: 10240 is longer than 10; brevity is not the reason.

choices.text: Memory comes in multiples of 256 MiB
choices.why: Right. A size like 10.25 GiB is valid, and MiB writes it as a whole number.

prompt: The sheet shows e2-small with 2 vCPUs. What does it actually guarantee?
hint: The 2 is a ceiling.

choices.text: Two whole vCPUs, exactly what an e2-standard-2 machine gets
choices.why: Then it would cost the same; it costs a quarter of that.

choices.text: Half a vCPU over time, bursting above it when there is room
choices.why: Right. The 2 is how far a burst reaches, not what is held for you.

choices.text: One vCPU, the same share as e2-medium
choices.why: e2-medium is the one with a whole vCPU.

choices.text: A quarter of a vCPU, the same as e2-micro
choices.why: A quarter is e2-micro's share.

prompt: A web server is busy every afternoon and has just been moved to e2-small "to save money". What will the team see, and where?
hint: What can a burst not cover?

choices.text: A higher bill, because bursting is charged by the second
choices.why: The price of e2-small is fixed; the cost of a sustained load is paid in speed.

choices.text: An error from Compute Engine refusing the move
choices.why: Nothing refuses it; the type is valid for any load.

choices.text: Slow afternoons, and nothing on the bill to explain them
choices.why: Right. A steady load is exactly what a burst cannot cover, and the bill does not say so.

choices.text: The machine restarting whenever it exceeds half a vCPU
choices.why: It is held to its share, not restarted.

prompt: Above 8 GiB per vCPU, an N4 custom type uses ___ memory, which is priced higher per GiB.
hint: Its name says it goes beyond the range.

prompt: Put the steps of choosing a machine type for a new service in the order this lesson argues for.
hint: The family comes before the size.
items: Measure the memory and processor the service uses under real load
Work out the ratio of memory to vCPU
Pick the family and type whose ratio matches
Pick the size, and compare a custom type only if the gap is large
trap: Picking a size first is the habit the lesson warns against: it lands on twice the vCPUs to get the memory.

prompt: Three copies of a service move from e2-standard-4 (0.13402284 USD an hour) to e2-highmem-2 (0.09039966). How much is saved in a month of 730 hours, to the cent?
hint: The hourly difference, times 730, times three.

prompt: Which of these does a clean terraform plan in this lab establish? Choose all that apply.
hint: A plan reads your file, not Google's catalogue.

choices.text: That the file is valid HCL the provider understands
choices.why: Right; that is what the provider checks.

choices.text: That the machine type exists in the zone
choices.why: e2-standard-3 planned cleanly and does not exist.

choices.text: Which attributes you set and which only Compute Engine can fill in
choices.why: Right; the second kind shows as (known after apply).

choices.text: That the project has quota for the machine
choices.why: Quota is checked by Google when the machine is created.
